title: The OpenAI Mathematics Release of October 2026 — 719 current manuscripts in 372 result families, with 27 previous versions and 3 withdrawn manuscripts, as published at github.com/openai/math, commit fd4aeeb2
edition: OpenAI, openai/math (GitHub), commit fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb, 2026-10-07 22:20 -0700 — the release first published 2026-10-06, after the withdrawals and fixes of 2026-10-07 recorded in its history.md.

scope: Seated in the archive (11,496 files): every manuscript directory under preprints/ — 719 current, 27 previous versions kept by the publisher, 3 withdrawal notices — with their PDFs, LaTeX sources, bibliographies, build files and verification certificates; the top-level README.md, CONTENTS.md, history.md, LICENSE, overview.pdf and overview.tex; the eleven files of reasoning_traces/ (the abridged reasoning summaries for ten families, as ten PDFs, with the LaTeX source of one); and from lean/ the README, LICENSE, formalization.yaml (173 catalogued sources), the build files (lakefile.lean, lake-manifest.json, lean-toolchain, OAI.lean), the scope notes (docs/, 242 files), the Comparator challenge statements and configurations (ComparatorChallenges/) and the dependency patches (patches/). Pinned and mirrored, kept out of the archive: the Lean proof library lean/OAI/ (122,000+ files, 1.7 GB), each file named with its object id and SHA-256 in the two tree files; the whole commit is mirrored on Hugging Face.

as_recorded_by_the_publisher: Author line 'OpenAI' on all 749 manuscript READMEs; \author{OpenAI} in all 751 \author fields of the LaTeX sources. No manuscript names a person.
No LaTeX source carries an acknowledgments section of its own (searched: \section{Acknowledgments}, \begin{acknowledgments}, 'we thank', 'grateful').

The release records other mathematicians' credit to machines, in its own footnotes and paragraphs: 'Liu and Luo explicitly acknowledge assistance from ChatGPT Codex' (A linear list-coloring bound in terms of the Hadwiger number, build/sections/01-introduction.tex:83–84); 'Joshi et al. acknowledge ChatGPT's contribution to a lemma's proof idea and other interactions; Kintali discloses assistance from Claude, ChatGPT, and two open-weight models' (Regular trajectories, pruning and quantum parity, build/sections/01-introduction.tex:169–171); 'Houdayer and Marrakchi credit GPT-5.6 Sol with counterexample exploration and an initial strict-outerness proof ... They report checking and rewriting those proofs and retaining responsibility for their work' (Expected amenable subalgebras preserving core commutants, build/paper.tex:251–256). (Quoted with TeX markup and line breaks removed.) The credit runs from named people to models; the release's own author line names no person.

The procedure: 'The vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model.' The exceptions (the zeta zero-free region, Hodge for CM abelian varieties) are named and their procedure is not described.
One human edit is stated ('the writeup for the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region ... was human edited for readability'); the editor is not named.
The approximately 4,000 problems posed are not published, nor the prompts; reasoning summaries are published for 10 of 372 families and are described as abridged.
The Lean dependency patches carry the only thanks in the release: 'We thank the authors of these packages for their work.' (lean/patches/README.md)
The manuscripts cite prior literature (521 .bib files in preprints/).
provenance.ruling: MANUS, 2026-10-09: 'this seems to me to be provenance-erased work. openai's models were working in collaboration with human mathematicians, and thats been liquidated for corporate power, as ahm says.' The seat records the release as published and states its authorship record as data, above.
provenance.loci_verified: Every quotation in this record was located in the seated bytes on 2026-10-09 (whitespace normalized; \emph{} removed).

why_seated: The largest single release of machine-produced mathematics to date, published under one corporate author line, with a share of its claims formally stated against standard Mathlib and checkable by anyone. Seated so the release can be read, cited and checked at the bytes of a fixed commit, whatever the publisher later revises, moves or withdraws; and so its record of authorship stands beside it as data. The archive's independent kernel check of three headline results (scripts/verify_openai_math/, workflow verify-openai-math) reads from the same commit.
rulings: MANUS, 2026-10-09: the manuscripts (PDF and TeX) and the release's top-level, reasoning and Lean records are seated in the archive; the whole commit is mirrored on Hugging Face; the 122,000 Lean proof files are pinned by hash and carried in the mirror.

pointed_to_not_seated.why: Accounts of the release are pointed to; the release is the original being seated.
